best_for: Photographers on Windows or Linux who shoot overlapping frames and want a free tool to stitch them into one panorama, with full control over control points and projection.

points.title: What it does
points.text: Hugin lines up a set of overlapping photos and blends them into a single panorama. It builds on Panorama Tools and the project calls it stable for everyday use.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: Hugin is released under the GNU GPL version 2 or later. There is no paid version and no account.

points.title: New in 2026.0
points.text: Version 2026.0.0 adds a graphical front end for image stacking in hugin_toolbox and anti-aliased options for shrinking output. The release notes advise keeping Hugin's own CPFind as the control point detector, since it is the only one the project endorses.

points.title: Mac users are stuck in 2019
points.text: The last official macOS build is 2019.2.0, for macOS 10.9 and later, and it does not run on Apple silicon. Nobody has volunteered to build an Arm version, so this page offers no Mac download.

points.title: Windows is 64-bit only
points.text: Current Windows releases come as a 64-bit MSI that installs for all users. The 32-bit line ended at 2017.0. The Windows listing keeps 6 versions.

points.title: Linux: Flatpak or your distro
points.text: The Flatpak listed here is on Flathub for x64 and Arm64, and Flathub does not mark it as verified by the Hugin team. Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu and others also package Hugin; only the current Flatpak release is listed here.
